goal: Be comfortable at salsa socials — know enough techniques, combine them, lead confidently

phases.name: Foundation — Basic Step, Right Turn, Hand Holds
phases.why: Everything starts here. Your instructor drilled quick-quick-slow rhythm, right turn footwork (forward-forward-turn, stay on the line), Spider-Man grip (2 fingers, no thumbs), leader signaling (lift on second bar), and spotting. Lock these in before adding anything new.

practice_sessions.focus: Basic step rhythm + right turn footwork (solo)
practice_sessions.drill:
WARM UP (5 min):
- 20 basics counting 'quick, quick, slow' out loud. Knees UP — 'up, up, up' not flat.
- Think drum beat: every foot hit = a beat.

RIGHT TURN FOOTWORK (10 min):
- 10 right turns solo: forward, forward, turn RIGHT. Land on right foot.
- KEY: Stay on the line — turn right but DON'T drift forward. Go right, back to center.
- After each turn, immediately basic: 'ta-ta-po' (back, back, forward).
- Full pattern: right turn → basic → right turn → basic. 10 reps.

SPOTTING (5 min):
- Pick a target on the wall. Eyes stay on it. Turn, bring head back to target.
- Do 10 right turns focusing ONLY on spotting. Don't worry about feet for these.

COOL DOWN:
- 10 basics with music, slow song. Just feel the rhythm.

BASICS WITH INTENT (5 min):
- 20 basics. On each one, say the count: 'back, back, forward, forward, forward, back' (leader timing).
- Make sure you're doing PART 2 FIRST as the leader.

LEADER SIGNAL DRILL (10 min):
- Air partner. Hold left hand up, 2 fingers (middle + ring, Spider-Man grip).
- Pattern: 1 basic → LIFT hand on second bar (this is the signal) → follower turns → 1 basic.
- Do 15 reps. Focus: the lift happens on count 1 of the second bar.
- Your forward does NOT change — you keep doing your basic while she turns.

HAND FLIP (5 min):
- Slow motion: cuff around fingers → flip wrist back as she turns → flip back down.
- 10 reps, just the hand movement. Then combine with the full signal drill.

LEADER'S OWN TURN (5 min):
- Forward, forward, turn. Left hand comes DOWN.
- Turn around, fingers rotate behind back, switch hand.
- 10 reps solo. Follower just does basic (imagine it).

practice_sessions.focus: Full combo with music — basic + right turn + leader turn
practice_sessions.drill:
SLOW SONG (15 min total):
- Put on a slow salsa song.
- Do 4 bars of basic.
- Right turn → basic.
- 4 more bars of basic.
- Leader's own turn → basic.
- Repeat the whole pattern for the full song.

GOAL: Never break timing. If you lose the count, stop, find the 1, restart.

CHECKLIST — ask yourself after each song:
- Was I on 'quick, quick, slow' the whole time?
- Did I stay on the line during turns?
- Did I spot a target?
- Was my hand hold relaxed (2 fingers, no death grip)?

Do 3 songs. If you nail all 3, you're ready for the next phase.

phases.name: Fundamental Variations — Angle, Side, Back
phases.why: These are variations on your basic step that give you more movement options on the dance floor. Same timing, different directions. They make your dancing look less robotic.

practice_sessions.drill:
REVIEW (3 min):
- 10 basics to warm up. Quick, quick, slow.

ANGLE BASIC (10 min):
- Same timing as regular basic but step at a 45-degree angle instead of straight back.
- 10 reps angling left, 10 reps angling right.
- Alternate: left angle → right angle → straight basic. 10 cycles.

SIDE STEP (10 min):
- Step to the side instead of back. Same quick-quick-slow timing.
- 10 reps stepping left, 10 reps stepping right.
- Combo: 2 basics → side step left → 2 basics → side step right. 10 cycles.

BACK STEP (10 min):
- Extended back step — reach further back than normal basic.
- 10 reps. Focus on full weight transfer.
- Combo: 2 basics → back step → basic. 10 cycles.

SIDE TO SIDE (10 min):
- Step side to side on the quick counts, hold on the slow.
- 10 reps each direction.
- This is a great fill move when you're not sure what to do next.

MIX IT UP (5 min):
- Slow song. Freestyle using ONLY basic + angle + side + back + side-to-side.
- Goal: smooth transitions, never break timing.

phases.name: Prep Step + Cross Body Lead
phases.why: The cross body lead is the second most important move after the basic — almost everything builds on it. The prep step sets it up. Once you have CBL, your vocabulary doubles.

practice_sessions.focus: Prep step + cross body lead breakdown
practice_sessions.drill:
PREP STEP (10 min):
- The prep step is how you signal the follower that a cross body lead is coming.
- Step to the side on count 1 to open the slot.
- 10 reps solo. Feel the difference from a straight basic.

CROSS BODY LEAD (15 min):
- Open on 1-2-3, she crosses on 5-6-7.
- Practice solo: step to the side to open the slot, then step back.
- 20 reps. Focus on creating a clear lane for the follower to walk through.
- Your feet: step side (1), collect (2), step back (3), then 5-6-7 basic.

CBL + BASIC COMBO (10 min):
- 4 basics → cross body lead → 4 basics → cross body lead.
- 10 cycles. Smooth transitions, don't rush the opening.

CBL + TURN COMBO (10 min):
- Basic → CBL → inside turn → basic → CBL.
- You now have a 4-move vocabulary. Combine freely.

FULL FREESTYLE (5 min):
- Slow song. Use everything: basic, angle, side, CBL, inside turn, right turn.
- Goal: never repeat the same pattern twice in a row.

phases.name: Footwork — Suzy Q, Fancy Basic, Tic Toc, Net Toe
phases.why: Footwork moves are what you do when you're not connected to a partner — shines. They make you look like you know what you're doing even when you're dancing solo. Great for musicality.

practice_sessions.drill:
SUZY Q (10 min):
- Cross one foot behind the other, swivel, repeat.
- Start slow: cross, swivel, cross, swivel. 10 reps each direction.
- Key: the swivel comes from your hips, not your feet.

FANCY BASIC (10 min):
- Adds a kick or flick to the basic step.
- Do 10 regular basics, then 10 fancy basics. Feel the difference.
- Don't overdo the flair — keep it subtle.

COMBO (5 min):
- 4 basics → Suzy Q (4 counts) → fancy basic → back to regular basic.
- 5 cycles with music.

TIC TOC (10 min):
- Weight shifts side to side, like a pendulum.
- 20 reps. Keep upper body still — movement is in the hips.
- Try with music: tic on the 1, toc on the 5.

NET TOE (10 min):
- Touch the toe out, bring it back. Alternating feet.
- 10 reps each side. Stay on time.

SHINE FREESTYLE (5 min):
- Song plays. No partner. Use all 4 footwork moves + basic.
- Goal: look comfortable, hit the breaks in the music.

phases.name: Transition + Check Basic
phases.why: Transition basic lets you switch between open and closed position smoothly. Check basic adds a pause-and-redirect move. These are connector techniques that make your combos flow.

practice_sessions.drill:
TRANSITION BASIC (10 min):
- Practice moving from closed position to open position mid-basic.
- 10 reps: closed → open. 10 reps: open → closed.
- Air partner. Focus on which hand releases and when.

CHECK BASIC (10 min):
- Step forward as if doing a CBL, then check (stop) and go back.
- 10 reps. The check is a clear signal — commit to the stop.
- Think of it as a fake-out: you start a move, then redirect.

COMBO (5 min):
- Basic → CBL → check basic → transition to open → basic.
- 5 cycles. Slow song.

phases.name: Crossbody Variations — She Goes, He Goes
phases.why: She Goes and He Goes are variations on the cross body lead where only one person crosses. They add variety and let you play with the follower's and leader's movement independently.

practice_sessions.drill:
SHE GOES (10 min):
- Like a CBL but only the follower moves across. Leader stays.
- 10 reps with air partner. Focus on the lead hand guiding her path.
- Signal is similar to CBL but your body stays in place.

HE GOES (10 min):
- Now YOU cross and she stays. Mirror of She Goes.
- 10 reps. The footwork is the same as CBL but you're the one walking through.

COMBO (5 min):
- Basic → She Goes → basic → He Goes → basic → regular CBL.
- 5 cycles. Slow song.

FULL CROSSBODY VOCAB (15 min):
- Slow song. You now have 4 crossbody moves: CBL, She Goes, He Goes, Check Basic.
- Freestyle: use all 4 plus basics, turns, and footwork.
- Goal: string together 3+ different moves without breaking timing.
- Try to use each crossbody variation at least twice per song.
- Do 3 songs.

phases.name: Turns — Copa, Sail Rights, Sail Lefts
phases.why: Copa is a direction change. Sail Rights and Sail Lefts are traveling turns that move the follower along the line. These are your Level 1 finale — once you have these, you have the full beginner vocabulary.

practice_sessions.drill:
COPA (10 min):
- The copa is a turn where the follower changes direction.
- Leader opens the door, follower walks in and turns back.
- 10 reps with air partner. Focus on clear hand signal.

SOMBRERO CROSSOVER (10 min):
- Arms go over the head (like putting on a sombrero) during a CBL.
- 10 reps. The arm goes over on the cross, comes back down after.
- Go SLOW — this is the most complex move so far.

SAIL RIGHTS (10 min):
- Traveling turn to the right. The follower moves along the line while turning.
- 10 reps. Keep the connection light — guide, don't pull.

SAIL LEFTS (10 min):
- Same concept but traveling left.
- 10 reps. Mirror image of sail rights.

COMBO (5 min):
- Basic → sail right → basic → sail left → copa → basic.
- 5 cycles.

THE FINAL DRILL (20 min):
- Put on 4 full salsa songs.
- Use EVERYTHING: basics (regular, angle, side, back, side-to-side, fancy), footwork (Suzy Q, tic toc, net toe), CBL family (CBL, she goes, he goes, check, sombrero), turns (inside, right, copa, sail right, sail left).
- Goal: never repeat the same 3-move sequence.
- Between songs, pick 2 moves that felt awkward and drill them 5 reps each.

YOU'RE READY FOR SOCIALS:
- If you can get through all 4 songs without losing timing, you have the vocabulary.
- At a social, you'll only use 5-6 of these per song. But knowing all 20 means you always have options.
